original_question: Can one establish general fundamental theorems of fractional calculus for fractional operators with distributed lag, especially in models where memory effects and distributed lag are present simultaneously?
target_in_paper: Section 4.2, "Economics with nonlocality in time: memory and distributed lag": the informal open problem that for the fractional operators with distributed lag proposed in [154] and used in the cited economic models, "the fundamental theorems of FC have not been proved in general," together with the remark that this is an important future-research direction. ([d-nb.info](https://d-nb.info/1258859653/34))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly captures both the mathematical gap and the application-driven motivation: Section 4.2 explicitly says that, in models where memory effects and distributed lag occur simultaneously, the missing issue is to prove general fundamental theorems of fractional calculus for fractional operators with distributed lag. ([d-nb.info](https://d-nb.info/1258859653/34))
missing_details: The paper is not speaking about arbitrary nonlocal fractional operators; it singles out distributed lag/time delay represented by Laplace-convolution operators whose kernels are probability density functions. ([d-nb.info](https://d-nb.info/1258859653/34))

The relevant domain is the positive real semi-axis R_+ = (0, infinity), not a finite interval; both the distributed-lag discussion and the general-FC comparison framework are phrased on this domain. ([d-nb.info](https://d-nb.info/1258859653/34))
The motivating scope is economic models with simultaneous memory and distributed lag, not merely distributed lag in isolation. ([d-nb.info](https://d-nb.info/1258859653/34))

To make "fundamental theorems of FC" stand-alone, one should specify that within this paper the natural benchmark is Section 2.3: left-inverse identities and reconstruction identities for general fractional integrals/derivatives, especially Theorems 5-6 and 8-9. ([d-nb.info](https://d-nb.info/1258859653/34))

The operator type is missing: the paper's internal formulations distinguish Riemann-Liouville-type and Caputo-type general fractional derivatives associated with a general fractional integral. ([d-nb.info](https://d-nb.info/1258859653/34))

Kernel hypotheses are missing: the comparable general setting in Section 2.3 uses kernel pairs (kappa,k) satisfying a Sonine or generalized Sonine convolution relation, with kappa in C_{-1}(0,infinity), k in C_{-1,0}(0,infinity), i.e. pairs in L_n. ([d-nb.info](https://d-nb.info/1258859653/34))

The natural function spaces are missing: C_{-1}(0,infinity), C_{-1,(k)}(0,infinity), and C_{-1}^n(0,infinity) are the spaces on which the paper states its analogue fundamental theorems. ([d-nb.info](https://d-nb.info/1258859653/34))

The paper points to a key tractable subclass that your draft omits: the gamma-distribution density is highlighted because it is a Sonine kernel, so the general-FC machinery can be used there (and for some other distributions on the positive semi-axis). ([d-nb.info](https://d-nb.info/1258859653/34))

The phrase "in general" should be tied to the class of fractional operators with distributed lag proposed in [154] and used in the cited economics references, rather than to every conceivable nonlocal operator. ([d-nb.info](https://d-nb.info/1258859653/34))
refined_question: For the fractional operators with distributed lag discussed in Section 4.2—namely Laplace-convolution operators on R_+ = (0,infinity) whose kernels are probability density functions and that are intended to model the simultaneous presence of memory and distributed lag in economics—can one prove general analogues of the first and second fundamental theorems of fractional calculus, in the sense made precise in Section 2.3? More specifically, determine natural hypotheses on the kernel pair (kappa,k) and on the corresponding function spaces on R_+ under which the associated general fractional integral I_(kappa) and the Riemann-Liouville- and/or Caputo-type general fractional derivatives D_(k) and *D_(k) satisfy left-inverse identities D_(k) I_(kappa) f = f and/or *D_(k) I_(kappa) f = f, together with second-fundamental-theorem identities of the form I_(kappa) *D_(k) f = f - sum_{j=0}^{n-1} f^(j)(0) h_(j+1) (and, where appropriate, I_(kappa) D_(k) f = f), for this distributed-lag class; in particular, can this be carried out for the gamma-distribution kernel and related kernels on the positive semi-axis? ([d-nb.info](https://d-nb.info/1258859653/34))
justification: This is the closest paper-faithful sharpening because this paper has no numbered conjecture or open-problem label for your target; the exact target is the informal statement in Section 4.2 on p. 3263 that the fundamental theorems of FC have not been proved in general for fractional operators with distributed lag. The only place where the paper itself spells out what "fundamental theorems of FC" means is Section 2.3, especially Theorems 5-6 and 8-9 on pp. 3253-3255, so those results supply the precise stand-alone content. Algebraic qualifiers such as homogeneity, degree, nilpotency, or "for all sufficiently large m" do not arise in this paper and therefore are not part of the faithful reformulation. ([d-nb.info](https://d-nb.info/1258859653/34))
